 4 Clippers Players Who Could Be Traded By The 2027 NBA Trade Deadline 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 The Los Angeles Clippers have had a tumultuous off-season, to say the least. Few teams lose a star player of Kawhi Leonard ‘s caliber and see the suspension of several important individuals within the team, including team owner Steve Ballmer, during the same off-season.
 However, regardless of their losses from the salary cap circumvention scandal, which resulted in Los Angeles losing five first-round picks and owner Steve Ballmer complying with a suspension , the Clippers roster did undergo a few more notable subtractions. Nic Batum , who had been with the team since 2020, barring his 2023-24 season with the Philadelphia 76ers, announced his retirement; Bogdan Bogdanovic and John Collins departed for the Houston Rockets and Detroit Pistons , respectively.
 However, the Clippers also made several pickups that could influence their 2026-27 season, including players such as Brandon Ingram , Gradey Dick , Max Strus , and Rui Hachimura .
 However, with an underwhelming 2-8 start to their season and projected to win just 28.6 games, could the Clippers be sellers at the trade deadline?
 MacMahon Names Los Angeles Clippers As Potential Sellers At The Trade Deadline
 According to ESPN’s Tim MacMahon, many scouts and executives league-wide have their eyes on the Clippers as ‘likely sellers’ at the trade deadline.
 “It’s way too early for trade discussions to pick up steam, but multiple scouts and executives are keeping an eye on the LA Clippers as likely sellers. The Clippers (…..) have a handful of impact veterans on expiring contracts. Center Brook Lopez , guard Kris Dunn , forward Rui Hachimura (team option next season), and wings Max Strus and Derrick Jones Jr. all could fill roles for playoff teams.”
 Ingram and Dick will be a part of the future for the Clippers, alongside Darius Garland , who was traded to the Clippers earlier this year. Ingram was ruled out with an injury to begin this season, as he recovers from right heel surgery and a partially torn Achilles tendon. The forward averaged 21.5 points, 5.6 rebounds and 3.6 assists last season as the primary offensive option for Toronto last season.
 Dick, who has played 10 games with the Clippers thus far this season, has upped his stats from the previous year and will come off the bench for the Clippers. Hachimura, who joined the Clippers this off-season, brings versatile scoring and three-point shooting, hitting 44.3% of his threes last season on 3.9 attempts a game. Lastly, 5th overall pick from the 2026 NBA Draft , Keaton Wagler , will be someone the Clippers will look to develop into a homegrown star, which means that he will not be up for grabs anytime soon.
 So, out of the players that the Clippers currently have, who are the ones who may find themselves on a different team by the time the trade deadline has passed?
 On The Trading Block?
 Nov 10, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Los Angeles Clippers forward Derrick Jones Jr. (5) against the Phoenix Suns in the first half at Mortgage Matchup Center. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images 
 It can be said with a fair amount of certainty that Lopez is one of the most likely players currently on the Clippers who could get traded. Despite being 38 and currently playing his 19th NBA season, Lopez remains an impactful veteran who can stretch the floor and provide decent rim protection.
 In 75 games for the Clippers last season, Lopez averaged 8.5 points, 3.6 rebounds, 1.3 assists, and 1.2 blocks. He also averaged 1.5 three-pointers made, attempting 4.2 perg game, shooting 36% from deep. While his age and expiring contract could deter teams, he may be a vital pick-up for teams that need a reliable back-up big man. However, the Clippers may not see a huge return from trading the ageing big man.
 Dunn is another player who may likely be traded, mostly due to his expiring contract. While currently a starter for the Clippers, impacting both ends of the floor, Dunn is set to be a free agent in the 2027 off-season. Dunn will be a valuable rotational piece on a contender looking to add depth, and a defensive-minded guard, with the NBA veteran averaging 1.6 steals per game and shooting 37.4% from the three last season.
 Jones Jr. is an athletic forward who can have a good defensive impact on a team, averaging 1.0 blocks and 0.9 steals per game last season. Strus is similar in size to Jones Jr., but has a much more offensively tuned game, averaging 40.2% on three-pointers last season. Both can potentially find a role for themselves on playoff teams, and their mid-sized contracts ($10.4 million for Jones Jr., and $16.6 million for Strus) which expire after this season open up the possibility for a sign-and-trade or a trade outright.
 The Last Word
 Seemingly, from the outside, it may appear that the Clippers are in a basketball purgatory of sorts post the Leonard era, which ended in scandal. With their 2028 first-round draft pick being owed to the 76ers, and the NBA penalizing them for Ballmer’s under-the-table arrangement to pay Leonard by seizing five first-round draft picks from 2029 to 2033, the future does look bleak for the other team in LA.
 However, the main asset that the Clippers have right now is their relative wealth of good rotational pieces who can be flipped to contenders. This includes teams such as the Oklahoma City Thunder, who have suffered from injuries this season, or the Denver Nuggets, who could use bench scoring and depth. Both teams have concerns that can be addressed by the players that the Clippers have.
 This is why the 2027 NBA trade deadline could be a crucial time for the Clippers; LA could possibly work out deals that help them gain first-round draft picks and build for their future. And if the Clippers play their cards right, what is ahead may not seem so bad after all.
